thread.title: Apple still undervalued: Here's why - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL)

author: Marry Schwarz
title: Apple still undervalued: Here's why - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL)
text:
12 Investment Thesis It's disconcerting to think that such a big company, with such a cult following as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) could see its shares almost double in a year. If the market is truly efficient, should a company add almost $ 450 billion in value in just 720 days? This article will argue that Apple shares, although it has seen an increase, are still undervalued. AAPL data of YCharts The summary Almost 2 million people have Apple in their portfolio in SeekingAlpha. It's the stock most often. It has the largest market capital of listed companies and will probably be the first company to reach a market limit of $ 1 trillion. However, he is still undervalued with all these eyes on him. Buffett can see it. He owns approximately 240 million shares. Here's why it's still undervalued. The narrative Apple, until a few years ago, depended on iPhone sales. Everything was about the iPhone. iPhone, iPhone, iPhone. Now it's all about the service segment. Instead of just focusing on phone sales, Apple has now created a complex ecosystem of services, which includes App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud and AppleCare. But you know, right? It is difficult to write a story in Apple that everyone does not yet know. And most likely, this article does not provide any detail that surprises you. But maybe a new perspective does the trick. By the Numbers The iPhone is still huge for Apple, do not get me wrong. In just the first two quarters of the year, iPhone sales barely reached $ 100 billion. That surely is nothing to sneeze. The segment even saw a 14% growth in revenue thanks to a higher average sale price of the updates for iPhone 8 and iPhone X. But as said, the real owner was the growth in services. This segment grew 31% year-over-year to $ 9.2 billion in the last quarter reported. Yes, it is true, $ 9.2 billion in the quarter. To put this in perspective, Adobe (NASDAQ: ADBE) made only $ 8 billion in sales … for the year. Apple's service segment dwarfs that number. The Apple administration set a goal of $ 50 billion in service revenue for 2020. If we annualize that $ 9.2 billion, we get almost $ 37 billion by the end of this year. Then it would require almost 35% annual growth to reach $ 50 billion from there. Obviously, this does not take into account any sequential growth during the rest of this year. However, it is a testament to how big the administration thinks the service segment can grow. To return it to Adobe, we'll use it as a proxy to value Apple's services because it also sells subscriptions and is a mature business location. Apple does not divide the margins of the services, so Adobe can be a reasonable substitute for the margin profile. In addition, Adobe's revenues grow at a 25% stage, similar to Apple's services. The profit margin of Adobe is at a huge 30%. Then, with $ 8 billion in revenue, you get about $ 2.4 billion in profits. Access a PE ratio of approximately 50 and get approximately your market capitalization, which is $ 120 billion. If we assume, $ 37 billion in revenues at the end of this year for services, using the same profit margins and the valuation metric as Adobe, the value at the end of this year is $ 555 billion. In addition, services grow even faster than Adobe sales. Calculations Ex. – $ 37 billion * 30% profit margin * 50 PE = $ 555 billion By eliminating Apple's net cash position from its market capitalization, we obtain a corporate value of $ 764 thousand millions. Ex.– capitalization of $ 909 billion – $ 145 billion in net cash = corporate value of $ 764 billion Now we can make a small analysis of the sum of the parts to determine how much the business rest market. Ex. – $ 764 billion business value – $ 555 billion worth of services = $ 209 billion remaining in value Source: Apple Data Summary Leftovers In the past four quarters, Apple has obtained $ 247 billion in revenue. If you subtract sales from the respective services, you get about $ 214 billion in sales. Therefore, the market is pricing Apple's sacred hardware with a huge 1x gain. And it's not like Apple does not have any pricing power. The company can continuously raise the prices of new models and think of new ideas. Also, on the last earnings call, Tim Cook stated that
"We have the best portfolio of products and services that he never had." Of course he's going to say that, but he still shows a sense of Trust in what they are doing from the perspective of a new product. To try to assess the remains of an earnings angle, Apple has had a gross margin of around 38% for some time. Presumably, the service segment increases that number, but considering that it only represents 14% of revenues, probably not too much. Then let's say 35% of gross margin. Clearly, Apple's hardware has pricing power. Operating expenses typically accounted for 12-14% of revenues, so we can estimate an operating margin of 26%. So, at $ 214 billion in sales, an operating margin of 26%, gives us almost $ 56 billion in EBIT. That tells us that the market is pricing hardware and other product segments at less than 4x EBIT. You read that right, 3.8 to be exact. Source: Apple Consolidated Financials For a company that has just issued another $ 100 billion in repurchases, a world-class brand, top-notch management and incredible employees, 4x EBIT on the sacred iPhone, Mac and iPad seems a little hard to believe. Granted, this scenario assumes that the service segment can continue its growth and a rich valuation, but it seems decently conservative. 10x EBIT seems reasonable, so it would get a value for the surplus of $ 560 billion. Add that to $ 555 in services and get $ 1.1 trillion in stock market capitalization, a 22% advantage for today's prices. Not bad for a company that has all eyes on it. Until the end You may see that Apple has a slightly different light, maybe not, but I hope your perspective has changed a bit. I think Apple has a bad reputation because it's so big. It's hard to imagine a $ 900 billion company doubling soon, but look, it almost did it in less than two years. As an investor, we do not get any extra points for degrees of difficulty. And that is precisely the reason why Apple will continue to do well. It is too easy, it is overlooked because it is followed so closely. Everyone thinks there is no advantage.
